key_insight: CURVE introduces a culturally diverse, multilingual benchmark for long-video reasoning, filling a major evaluation gap caused by Western- and English-centric datasets with high-quality, human-generated annotations.
problem_solved: Existing long-video benchmarks are biased toward Western content and English language, limiting evaluation of models' ability to reason about cultural context and multilingual inputs.
method: Curate a balanced collection of long videos spanning multiple regions, cultures, and languages to reduce Western/English bias.
Annotate videos with high-quality, human-generated labels targeting long-range reasoning skills (temporal, causal, and culture-aware questions).
Provide an evaluation suite and metrics designed to test multilingual and cultural reasoning capabilities across lengthy video contexts.
impact: CURVE enables fairer, more robust evaluation of video models on cultural and multilingual reasoning, guiding researchers to build models that generalize beyond Western/English data and better serve global populations.
visual_elements: World map heatmap showing geographic distribution of videos and languages covered
Timeline/long-video schematic illustrating temporal and long-range reasoning tasks
Bar or radar chart comparing cultural/language diversity between CURVE and prior benchmarks
Icon set depicting task types (temporal reasoning, causal inference, cultural context, multilingual QA)
paper_title: CURVE: A Benchmark for Cultural and Multilingual Long Video Reasoning
paper_authors: Darshan Singh, Arsha Nagrani, Kawshik Manikantan, Harman Singh, Dinesh Tewari
